_comment: Items that must not pass `leveltest:distractors`. Each one shipped, or nearly shipped, and each names the rule that now stops it. `scripts/level-test-distractor-qa.mjs` runs every fixture through the same checks it runs over the bank and fails if any fixture passes — a gate that cannot fail is not a gate. `fixed` is the corrected form where one exists, and it must pass. Added 2026-09-10.

fixtures.why: The photographed item. Three of the four options are from unrelated conceptual categories, so the question is answerable by elimination without knowing 빛; and 아침 빛 is not the collocation a Korean speaker uses.
A bare noun blank modifying the noun behind it. 녹색 가방 and 흰색 가방 are bought as readily as 갈색 가방, so the item has three right answers.
A time noun in a 에 slot in front of an activity that can happen at any time. 월요일에 바다에 가요 is ordinary Korean.
A destination slot. Every place is a place one goes on a Sunday, so the builder had to reach outside the category for wrong answers and produced 장난 and 평화.
An existential frame. Anything at all can be on this evening.
A general verb with the blank as the sentence's only argument. A ball, a present and a window are all bought new.
Read and refused by a person: 편의점에서 채소를 사요 is true of Korean convenience stores, so the item has two answers no rule can separate.
Two options that a learner reads as one. Normalising away spacing and punctuation makes 비빔밥 and '비빔밥.' the same string, so the item has three choices wearing four labels.

fixed.why: The card's sentence, rewritten to the collocation Korean actually uses. It ships as a word card; it is refused as a gap-fill by F-07's mechanism, because everything that comes in through a window is a second answer.
A general verb is fine when the sentence carries a second argument that decides the answer: 밥 is what makes 쌀 the only option.
